content: Elafibranor is indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in adults. It is used in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) for patients who have had an inadequate response to UDCA or as monotherapy for those unable to tolerate UDCA. The recommended dosage is 80 mg orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of elafibranor have not been fully established. When co-administered with atorvastatin, elafibranor may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of creatine phosphokinase (CPK) elevation and/or myalgia. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Cholestyramine, colesevelam, and colestipol reduce elafibranor levels by binding the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Elafibranor should be administered at least 4 hours before or after taking a bile acid-binding sequestrant, or at the longest interval possible. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate, drospirenone, ethinyl estradiol, levonorgestrel (oral or transdermal), and norgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Elafibranor, when combined with statins such as fluvastatin, lovastatin, pitavastatin, pravastatin, rosuvastatin, or simvastatin, may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs elevate the risk of CPK elevation and/or myalgia. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases elafibranor levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Common adverse effects of elafibranor include weight gain (23%), diarrhea (11%), abdominal pain (11%), nausea (11%), vomiting (11%), arthralgia (8%), constipation (8%), muscle pain (7%), fractures (6%), gastroesophageal reflux disease (6%), dry mouth (5%), weight loss (5%), rash (5%), dizziness (≤5%), gastroenteritis (≤5%), increased blood creatinine (≤5%), anemia (≤5%), CPK elevation >3x ULN (4%), myalgia (4%), cholelithiasis (3%), and rare cases of rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury (1%). Based on animal reproduction studies, elafibranor may cause fetal harm when administered during pregnancy. There is insufficient data from human pregnancies to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. A negative pregnancy test should be verified before initiating treatment in females of reproductive potential. Pregnancies should be reported to Ipsen Pharmaceuticals. Patients are advised not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 weeks after the last dose due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants. Elafibranor is extensively metabolized to form a major active metabolite (GFT1007) via cytosolic enzyme 15-ketoprostaglandin 13-reductase (PTGR1). GFT1007 is further metabolized by CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and UGT2B7. Elafibranor is also metabolized by CYP2J2 and UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) isoforms UGT1A3, UGT1A4, and UGT2B7. The total clearance of elafibranor is 50 L/hr. Elafibranor can be taken with or without food. It should be stored at 15–30°C (59–86°F) in its original packaging to protect it from moisture and light.
